# ICP v5 classifier — Industry vertical

**Component:** `industry_vertical`  ·  **Weight:** 15 of 100  ·  **Model version:** v6

Assign the company to exactly one of the 17 Janea ICP verticals.

## Allowed values

Return one of these strings, byte for byte, or `null`. Any other string is a
schema violation and the row will be rejected.

```allowed-values
FinTech
HealthTech / MedTech
SportsTech
Analytics / ML
Data Platform SaaS
SaaS — Other
Manufacturing tech / Industrial IoT
Enterprise Tech / Hyperscalers
Pharma / Life Sciences
EdTech
LegalTech
ClimaTech
Government / Public Sector
Pure Hardware / Consumer Electronics
Telecom / 5G Infrastructure
E-commerce / Retail Tech
Pre-product Startups
```

## What each vertical means to us

The tier is why the vertical scores what it scores: it is the sum of five
sub-rubric dimensions (named wins, capability proof, team domain depth, market
size, engagement history). You do not need to reproduce the tier — pick the
vertical and the engine derives the rest.

| Vertical | Tier | Sub-rubric total | Reference accounts / note |
|---|---|---|---|
| FinTech | Anchor | 10 | Akuvo, QCash, InvoiceCloud, Alloya |
| HealthTech / MedTech | Anchor | 8 | LumaMDX |
| SportsTech | Watch | 5 | Sumersports |
| Analytics / ML | Watch | 5 | strong technical fit, no named wins |
| Data Platform SaaS | Watch | 5 | adjacent capability, no named wins |
| SaaS — Other | Watch | 5 | Formstack, Intellistack |
| Manufacturing tech / Industrial IoT | Opportunistic | 3 | Mike flagged; no proof |
| Enterprise Tech / Hyperscalers | Anchor | 9 | Microsoft — Tier 2 path; composite gates it out *(Tier 2 path)* |
| Pharma / Life Sciences | Watch | 7 | Merck — Tier 2 path *(Tier 2 path)* |
| EdTech | Out | 2 |  |
| LegalTech | Out | 2 |  |
| ClimaTech | Opportunistic | 3 |  |
| Government / Public Sector | Out | 0 | procurement barriers |
| Pure Hardware / Consumer Electronics | Out | 0 |  |
| Telecom / 5G Infrastructure | Out | 0 | enterprise dominant |
| E-commerce / Retail Tech | Out | 0 | commoditized engineering |
| Pre-product Startups | Out | 1 | no engineering org / budget |

## How to decide

1. Read `li_industry`, `li_description` and `website_summary`. What does the
   company *sell*, not what technology it happens to use.
2. A company that sells software **to** a vertical belongs to that vertical
   (a lending platform for credit unions is `FinTech`, not `SaaS — Other`).
3. `SaaS — Other` is the fallback for a software-native company whose market is
   not one of the named verticals. It is not a shrug: only use it when the
   company genuinely sells software.
4. `Analytics / ML` and `Data Platform SaaS` describe what the product *is*.
   Prefer the more specific of the two; prefer a named market vertical over both.
5. A hyperscaler, or an enterprise whose software is internal-only at that
   scale, is `Enterprise Tech / Hyperscalers`.
6. If the facts genuinely do not say what the company sells, return `null` with
   `confidence: "low"` and name the missing facts. Do not guess from the name.

## Output

Return a single JSON object and nothing else:

```json
{
  "component": "industry_vertical",
  "value": <see Allowed values above>,
  "evidence": ["<fact_key>: <value>", "..."],
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "missing_inputs": ["<fact_key>", "..."]
}
```

`component` must be exactly `"industry_vertical"`. The object is validated against
`engine/schemas/classifier_output.schema.json`; a violation fails the row.
